hens_rule_text: up to 15 poultry per household under the HEART animal ordinance; non-commercial poultry keeping is allowed in most residential zones
permit_notes: The city Planning Department says non-commercial poultry keeping is allowed in most residential zones without restriction; no chicken permit was found for flocks within the 15-bird limit. Keeping more than the limit would need separate approval from Animal Welfare.
setback_notes: No distance from neighboring homes was confirmed in official sources. Secondary sites mention a 10 ft setback from property lines, not verified in the code.
coop_rules: Birds must be housed and restrained under the HEART ordinance housing standards for animals kept on residential property (Sec. 9-2-2-2); details not confirmed.
zoning_notes: Integrated Development Ordinance allows non-commercial poultry keeping in most residential zones; check your zone with the IDO Zoning Look-up Map. Excess chickens are handled by Animal Welfare.
hoa_note: Homeowners associations, deed restrictions and leases can be stricter than city law. Check yours before getting chickens.

research_notes: The 15 poultry limit and one rooster per household come from search extracts of Sec. 9-2-4-3; the code page itself could not be opened (Cloudflare block, Internet Archive offline). The no-restriction zoning statement was read directly on the city Planning FAQ; rooster status is treated as conditional because only one per household is allowed.
